text: Plan a fair test by saying what to change, what to keep the same and what to watch
Carry out the planned test with the teacher and classmates and mark what happened
Compare how a gentler and a harder push or pull change how an object starts and moves
Compare pushes in different directions and how they change which way an object goes
Tell that a touch is what changes the motion of an object when two objects meet
Use the marks from the tests, keeping every try, to say what changed an object's motion
Observe the weather in the same place at two times of day and mark what is seen and felt
Share what dated daily records show, counting each date once
Describe the pattern a whole month of records shows, and where it varies
Ask a question that a forecast page can answer, to find out why people forecast the weather
Obtain the answer to a question from a forecast page or a second source
Use records of past storm days and today's page to say where and when storms are possible
Say what the school does before a storm and where it goes when thunder is heard
Ask a question, from what you watch, that a card or a safe demonstration can answer
Watch the ball and gather information, such as where it stopped and what the goal card says
Say the problem as what people want to be different, not as a thing to build
Say that we find out what is wanted before we build
Watch two pushes leave the line and judge whether a change made the ball start faster
Draw the path before and after a touch and judge whether a bumper turned the ball the wanted way
Say whether a design did what it was meant to do, using the result picture
Say that plants and animals both take in water, and point to the picture that shows it
Say that the plant records show light, and point to the plant that had it
Say that animals eat and a plant is not fed a meal, from the pictures
Say that different animals eat different foods, and match each animal to its food
Draw lines from a plant to what its place gives it, and put it where it can get them
Draw lines from an animal to what its place gives it, and put it where it can get them
Draw lines from people to the water, food, wood and air a place gives them
Point to a part of a place a plant changed, and say I think, because I saw
Point to a part of a place an animal changed, and say I think, because I saw
Compare two ways people change land and say which leaves more living things in place, and why
Choose the pair that is fair for finding out what the sun does: the same material, put out for the same time, one sunny and one shaded
Mark which of a sunny and a shaded sample felt warmer, or about the same, for sand, soil, rock and water
Say that a sunny sample was warmer than its shaded match at one look, so the sun warmed it, and not the clock
Choose a cover that sits over the spot and keeps the sun off it, and name the roof as the part that does it
Use the given paper, cardboard and tape to build a cover over the spot and say how it should help
Compare a covered patch with its open match and say, from what was felt, whether the cover kept the warming down
Say or point to what people do in a place and which part of it changes because of that: land, water, air or a living thing
Draw a way people could act so the place is harmed less, and what it would change
Tell a partner why the drawn action lessens the harm, using the drawing
